population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: ever 37.0% − current 27.9% = 9.1% of adults used and are off now. The 10.5 pts of new ever-users since 2030 split into 8.0 on and 2.5 already off. Of the 26.5 pts who had used by 2030, 19.9 are on and 6.6 are off. On: 8.0 + 19.9 = 27.9. Off: 2.5 + 6.6 = 9.1. Within the 2030 cohort: 11.3 of the 18.8 then on stayed on (60%, up from ~50% in 2028–30 because conditional coverage penalises stopping and the price fell). The 7.5 who stopped joined the 7.7 already off, making a pool of 15.2. Of those, 8.6 restarted (57% over two years, in line with the parent's 55%), so 11.3 + 8.6 = 19.9 on and 15.2 − 8.6 = 6.6 off. Cycled: the 8.9 pts who had cycled by 2030, plus ~4.0 pts of first-time restarters in the 2030 cohort and ~0.5 among new starters, give 13.4 of 37.0 ever-users = 36%. Current users ≈ 74.8M of ~268M adults. Age bands weighted by adult shares (20/33/24/23%): 3.2 + 10.23 + 10.56 + 3.91 = 27.9. Income thirds: (34 + 28 + 21.7)/3 = 27.9. The 18–29 band rose most in relative terms (10→16) through the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program, police and fire contracts, and cheaper oral starts. The 65+ band rose only 12→17 (~10.5M) despite the dementia-risk label, because the bone wave and Bridge DEXA conditions slowed it. Bottom-third use reached 21.7% through conditioned Medicaid, HRSA free provision and $149 oral starts, and remains mostly lower-efficacy product. Off-drug: ~24.4M adults have used and stopped, many of them cut off by conditioning rules (missed weigh-ins, lack of BMI progress) rather than by choice. ~169M have never used: a mix of deliberate refusers, now an organised constituency, the uninsured in non-expansion states, and people with contraindications. Pediatric: 1.2% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 880k, of whom ~150k are aged 6–11. The first registry bone data arrived in 2032 (see ledger). A cohort of children has now grown up eating at tables where at least one parent is on a drug.

access.public_coverage: The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge was renewed in Dec 2031 through 2033. Payment falls from $275 to $225/month from Jan 2032 under the Strategic Supply Agreement pricing. The copay stays $50. Continuation is now conditional: ≥5% weight loss by month 6, ≥80% PDC, and for 65+ a baseline and annual DEXA plus a documented resistance-training referral. About 3.4M beneficiaries use it for obesity: 3.4M × $225 × 12 ≈ $9.2B/yr. Medicare overall pays ≈14.7% of incretin fills ≈ 11.0M users (≈10.5M adults 65+ plus ~0.5M disabled under-65). Medicaid pays ≈12% ≈ 9.0M users at $225: 9.0M × $225 × 12 ≈ $24.3B/yr combined federal and state. Seven states run Indiana-style adherence waivers: Indiana and Arkansas, plus Missouri, Oklahoma, Georgia, Ohio and Montana. The HRSA Community Incretin Access Program received $5.0B in FY2032 and is still unconditional (refill pickup only). It serves ≈3.6M: 2.4M generic liraglutide × $70 × 12 = $2.0B, plus 1.2M semaglutide for cessation/AUD × $179 × 12 = $2.6B, ≈ $4.6B. TRICARE, the VA and the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program cover ≈2.4M, including ~140k active-duty members in the readiness programme: 140k × $149 federal price × 12 ≈ $250M/yr.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 80+ semaglutide brands at $7–40/month, and generic tirzepatide has launched in India, Brazil and Turkey. Generic semaglutide is sold across Canada, Mexico, China and most of Latin America and Asia. Chinese originator triple agonists are approved domestically by the NMPA. US generic semaglutide entry dates are set by patent settlements for 2033. Tirzepatide remains protected to the mid-2030s.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~74.8M users: commercial 38.5% (28.8M), Medicare 14.7% (11.0M), Medicaid 12% (9.0M), HRSA free 4.8% (3.6M), TRICARE/VA/DoD 3.2% (2.4M), cash/direct 14.8% (11.1M), gray 12% (9.0M) = 100%. Managed decline: the March 2031 Strategic Supply Agreement and Novo's matching deal stepped TrumpRx/direct prices down to $249 (semaglutide injection), $299 (tirzepatide), $149 (oral starting doses: Wegovy pill, Foundayo) and $399 (retatrutide, newly unallocated). Wegovy list stays $1,349 and retatrutide list $1,499. Almost nobody pays list. Coverage is the rationing tool. Employer weight-management coverage rose from 57% to 63%, but ~55% of covering employers now attach conditions: PBM-verified ≥80% PDC, ≥5% loss at 6 months, and coaching enrollment. Some add premium differentials of up to 30% under the 2031 tri-agency outcomes-based wellness guidance, which accepts PBM adherence data as a 'reasonable alternative standard'. Gray users are flat at ~9M in absolute terms. Expanded Section 232 duties and CBP seizure of Indian mail pens squeezed imports, but 503A 'personalised' compounders ($99–199) switched part of their API sourcing. Research-peptide retatrutide shrank once the branded product hit $399. Conditioning has produced a 'skip-but-fill' pattern: users pick up refills to keep PDC above 80% while taking dose holidays, which degrades adherence data as a clinical signal.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Next-gen driver realised through an existing product in a new form: FDA approved a retatrutide 12 mg maintenance dose in Jun 2031 on TRIUMPH-4 extension data (30.4% mean loss at 104 weeks in the efficacy estimand). Lilly's new Virginia API plant then lifted allocation. MariTide (BLA Jul 2030) was approved Sep 2031 with limited launch supply, ~0.6M users. Survodutide, resubmitted after its 2029 CRL, was approved Nov 2031 narrowly for obesity with MASH F2–F3. Amycretin was resubmitted in 2031 after Novo's facility remediation and is under review, with a decision in 2033. Bimagrumab + tirzepatide (phase 3) filed a BLA in Mar 2032 under muscle-wave pressure; it is not on the market and the decision is not before 2033. The dementia label rests on a confirmatory randomised prevention trial in metabolic-risk adults (HR ~0.82 for all-cause dementia, weighted toward vascular and mixed dementia) and adjudicated SELECT/SOUL follow-up. The 2025 EVOKE failure in established Alzheimer's still stands, and the label says so. The incretin market is ≈$165B globally in 2032: US volume +49% and US net price −15 to −20%.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Rates are higher on the retatrutide 12 mg dose and among gray users who skip titration.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Delayed emptying on drug is established; persistence after stopping is still disputed. MDL 3094 has ~61,000 filed and tolled claims. Three of five bellwethers went to plaintiffs, and there is no global settlement.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled. FDA still declines to label persistent gastroparesis. Reserves raised in 2031 annual reports.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Absolute cases rise with retatrutide 12 mg and faster loss.
Large registries still show low absolute risk with no causal confirmation. The pancreatitis track in the MDL grows anyway.

Recognised as a population problem. NHANES-DXA 2029–31 shows appendicular lean mass in 65+ users more than 2 years on drug ~0.5 SD below matched non-users, with sarcopenia criteria met at ~1.6× the rate. It is worst on liraglutide and compounded product without protein or resistance-training support.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings section strengthened (Sep 2031). Bridge continuation requires a resistance-training referral. HRSA sites have no requirement, and a HELP letter asks why. Bimagrumab combination filed.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Population-visible. Medicare hip-fracture admissions rose ~4% in 2030–31, the first rise in two decades. Modelled excess ≈ 10.5M users 65+ × ~0.5%/yr baseline × HR 0.35 ≈ 18,000 hip fractures a year, concentrated in women and cyclers. The adolescent registry interim (2032) shows lumbar-spine BMD z-score accrual ~0.2 SD lower after more than 3 years on drug. That is unadjudicated and disputed as confounded by weight loss itself.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA class safety-labelling change (Sep 2031): baseline DEXA for 65+ and postmenopausal women in the Warnings section (not boxed). AACE/Endocrine Society endorse antiresorptive co-prescription in high-risk users. Bridge mandates DEXA. FDA requests a pediatric labelling update pending the final bone-accrual study.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still conflicting cohorts; very low absolute risk.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare'; FDA warnings mention unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association, including in the BED and AUD populations.

Retatrutide postmarketing results (Apr 2031): clinically meaningful SHAPS anhedonia shift in ~8% at ≥8 mg vs ~4% on comparator, dose-dependent. Surveys of long-term users across agents hold at ~10–15% reduced pleasure. About 45% of long-term users report at least one deliberate dose holiday in the past year.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 'Reduced pleasure/anhedonia' added to the retatrutide Adverse Reactions section (Aug 2031) and as a class precaution for doses above maintenance. The same pharmacology is the basis of the Jun 2032 BED approval. FTC continues to police 'calm/focus' claims by non-manufacturers.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Increasingly driven by conditioning cut-offs: Bridge 6-month non-responders, Medicaid lockouts and employer BMI-progress failures.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation unresolved; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Protein, iron, B12 and vitamin D insufficiency signals strengthen. Protein intake is now seen as the link to the muscle wave.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; Bridge counselling includes a protein target.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of follow-up in adults and nine in adolescents. ~150k children aged 6–11 are on drug. Pubertal-timing data are still absent.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric registry ongoing; bone-accrual interim under FDA review.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Poison-centre incretin calls are flat at 2030 levels. Research-retatrutide cases fell after the $399 branded price, while compounded-semaglutide dosing errors persist.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CBP pharmaceutical mail seizures under the Section 232 expansion; ~60 warning letters; first federal indictment of a peptide distributor (2032), not of users.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg.
Prescribing for 'brain health' in people outside the label (no diabetes, no CVD) is growing fastest among 50–64-year-olds, who carry the bone risk without proven cognitive benefit.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA labelling states the population limits. No enforcement against off-label prescribing.

food_and_beverage.state: With more than one adult in four on drug, US packaged-food volume falls ~2.5% a year. Snacks and confectionery are hit hardest. Majors finish selling indulgent brands to private equity and regional owners. Protein, fibre and now 'bone-and-muscle' formats (calcium, leucine, vitamin D) grow, sold as companions to Bridge counselling.

alcohol.state: AUD coverage plus a quarter of adults on appetite-reducing drugs keep US spirits and beer volume falling for a fourth year. Distillers lean on exports and premium single-serve formats. State excise forecasts now carry an explicit incretin line.

restaurants.state: Value-volume chains keep closing units in mid-income suburbs. Fast casual sells 'half plates' at near-full price. Military-town restaurants near Fort Bragg and Fort Hood report smaller checks. Church-hall potlucks and 'open table' suppers from the backlash movement are a small countercurrent with no measurable effect on sales.

apparel.state: Size runs keep widening. Workwear and uniform makers re-cut for leaner police and military bodies. Hip-protector and fall-safe apparel enters mainstream senior catalogues.

fitness.state: Resistance training is now prescribed. Bridge referrals and employer conditions feed low-cost gyms, physical-therapy chains and Medicare Advantage strength programmes. The research-peptide gym trade shrinks as branded retatrutide gets cheaper.

insurance.state: Pharmacy trend slows to ~+9% as net prices fall and volume rises. Plans manage cost through conditions rather than exclusions: adherence gates, BMI-progress gates and premium differentials. PBMs sell adherence-verification as a service. Litigation over wellness differentials is pending in two circuits.

pharma.state: Lilly is the designated national champion: tariff-exempt, DPA-financed, and the federal price setter. Novo matches on price and absorbs tariff on Danish API, so margin compresses. Generic liraglutide makers hold HRSA contracts. US exposure to Indian API is now a board-level risk at compounders. MDL reserves are rising.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body now carries a payer's conditions as well as a molecule. A lean body with muscle and a DEXA history reads as compliant: Bridge-renewed, employer-qualified, tape-passed. A heavier body reads three ways: cut off by a missed condition, priced out, or refusing on principle. The last is now a public identity, not an excuse.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The 'Charlotte build' has spread down-market as retatrutide fell to $399, so muscle has become the marker. Retatrutide without training produces thin, soft bodies, and coaches call it 'pen-thin'. Among women 65+ in Sun City, Arizona, the visible class marker is posture and a fall-free year: the affluent buy antiresorptives, protein and twice-weekly trainers; others get a referral slip.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: A counter-ritual has formed. 'Open Table' suppers, started in Grand Rapids church networks and copied in Nashville and Tulsa, frame shared full meals as fellowship against 'pharmaceutical fasting'. Fat-liberation groups in Oakland and Brooklyn run 'unmedicated' supper clubs. Family-doctor guidance on 'kid portions' now includes children watching parents skip meals.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list the molecule, and some list 'drug-free since 2029' as a value, not a confession. Couples where one partner is on a conditioned employer plan negotiate dose holidays around the plan's adherence window.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is clinical and, through coverage, contractual. The backlash reclaims it as moral or sacred: 'hunger is how we were made' is a sermon line and a bumper sticker. Two states (Tennessee, Idaho) passed laws barring employers from conditioning premiums on incretin use, framed as 'appetite liberty'.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Validated retatrutide data (Apr 2031) put clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~8% vs ~4% at high doses. Across agents ~10–15% of long-term users report reduced pleasure. About 45% of long-term users report at least one deliberate dose holiday in the past year, and conditional coverage pushes many of these into 'skip-but-fill'. Low-dose Foundayo for BED (approved Jun 2032) had ~0.9M users by year-end, inside the commercial and cash shares. Telehealth wellness 'quiet' subscriptions fell from ~2M to ~1.3M as the FTC acted and the complaint went mainstream.
interior_life.framing: A complaint and a treatment at once. 'The grey' is everyday vocabulary, and late-night monologues joke about it. Pharmacists ask 'are you holidaying this month?' The same effect is advertised for BED as 'quiet the noise around food'. Clinicians say 'dose-dependent reward modulation'. The backlash says 'chemical contentment'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employers have stopped marketing 'focus' perks after the FTC and union pushback. Conditioned benefit plans still make adherence a workplace variable. Sales staff time holidays to quarter-end. Military and police programmes track tape, weight and DEXA, not mood, though Army chaplains report soldiers describing 'the grey' at counselling.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' is now a common billing, not a niche one, and some festivals sell 'holiday weekend' passes timed to when users skip. Comedy built on the grey is a genre. Sports-betting and casino operators cite reduced handle in earnings calls again.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Dose holidays around anniversaries and conception attempts are routine. Sex therapists now cite the retatrutide label section directly. Partners on mismatched conditioned plans argue over whose adherence window governs the holiday.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Two blocs cut across party. Pro-access populists defend TrumpRx prices and readiness programmes. An anti-pharma, religious and fat-liberation coalition opposes conditioning, the military programme and 'calm marketing'. Candidates are asked if they are on, and lately whether they take holidays. Turnout effects are still unmeasured.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access and price-managing. It approves new indications (BED, dementia risk, MASH) and new forms (retatrutide 12 mg, MariTide), and acts on bone and muscle through labelling rather than restriction. Gray-market enforcement has shifted from letters to customs seizures and one indictment.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate to take the drug. Subsidy channels: the Medicare Bridge ($225/$50, conditional), the HRSA programme ($5.0B FY2032, unconditional), the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program, and the ACA cessation mandate (two 90-day courses a year). The Strategic Supply Agreement ties federal prices to Lilly's tariff exemption.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Conditioning is now the dominant access tool. Seven Medicaid adherence waivers. Bridge continuation tied to 6-month response, PDC and DEXA. Employer outcomes-based wellness plans use PBM adherence feeds and premium differentials. Tennessee and Idaho ban premium conditioning. HRSA remains the unconditioned exception, and plaintiffs and critics cite it from both sides.
state.workforce_or_military: The DoD Metabolic Readiness Program (May 2031) offers tirzepatide or semaglutide through military treatment facilities to service members who fail body-composition standards: ~140k active duty, plus Guard pilots. Body-composition failure separations fell ~30% in FY2032. The FAA streamlined special issuance for pilots on stable doses. Big-city police and fire contracts (Phoenix, Houston, Chicago) cover drugs for fitness-standard compliance. DOT apnea clearance still runs through tirzepatide. About 1,900 religious-accommodation requests to decline the readiness programme have been filed. Participation is formally voluntary, but separation for failing standards is not.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Incretins are designated critical medicines under Section 232 Phase II (Mar 2031), with duties extended to API and peptide intermediates. Lilly is the national champion, with tariff exemption and Defense Production Act Title III financing for its Virginia and Texas plants in return for federal ceiling prices and priority supply to DoD and VA. Novo pays duty on Danish API amid broader US–Denmark friction. India's mail exports are seized at the border, and India files a WTO consultation request. Chinese controls on protected amino-acid exports (Aug 2031) raised compounder costs. Global South markets run on Indian generics.

events.event: Commerce expands Section 232 pharmaceutical duties to incretin APIs and peptide intermediates and designates Eli Lilly a 'strategic supply' national champion: tariff exemption and DPA Title III loans in exchange for federal ceiling prices. TrumpRx steps down to $249 for semaglutide, $299 for tirzepatide and $149 for oral starts as Novo matches

Pentagon launches the Metabolic Readiness Program offering tirzepatide or semaglutide at military treatment facilities to service members failing body-composition standards; FAA streamlines pilot special issuance; chaplains begin forwarding religious-accommodation requests
FDA approves a 12 mg retatrutide maintenance dose showing 30.4% mean weight loss at two years; Lilly ends allocation and lists a $399 direct price as its Virginia API plant comes online

CMS data show the first rise in Medicare hip-fracture admissions in two decades; FDA orders class labelling that puts baseline DEXA for older users and postmenopausal women in the Warnings section, and endocrine societies endorse routine antiresorptive 'bone cover'

Congress renews the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge through 2033 at $225/month with continuation tied to 5% weight loss at six months, 80% adherence and annual DEXA; days later Labor, HHS and Treasury guidance lets employer wellness plans use PBM adherence data for premium differentials

FDA approves low-dose orforglipron for binge-eating disorder, which Lilly markets with the line 'quiet the noise around food', and in the same month approves semaglutide to reduce dementia risk in adults 55 and over with diabetes or obesity plus cardiovascular disease

open_tensions: The dementia-risk label pulls older adults onto the drug just as the bone wave makes them the group it harms most visibly. Medicare now pays for both the incretin and the antiresorptive, and nobody has trial data on the combination's fracture outcome in 75+.

Conditional coverage depends on adherence data, while dose holidays for the mainstream 'grey' complaint push users into skip-but-fill. That makes the PBM adherence feeds behind Bridge, Medicaid waivers and employer premiums increasingly fictional, and the wellness-differential cases in two circuits may decide whether they can be used at all.

The national-champion deal lowered prices by tying federal supply to one company. India's WTO challenge, Novo's tariff burden and US generic semaglutide entry dates in 2033 all threaten the bargain before the Bridge expires.

The military readiness programme and employer premium conditions have given the backlash coalition concrete grievances and two state laws. The HRSA programme, which has no conditions, is attacked by conditioning advocates as waste and by the backlash as 'pacification', and its FY2033 rider is not guaranteed.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is sold in the US.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The ACA preventive mandate still requires plans to cover semaglutide for smoking cessation in two 90-day courses a year.

prose.headline: Lighter, Cheaper, Conditional: 75 Million Americans on the Pen, and Their Bones Are Starting to Show the Bill
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2032 more than one American adult in four is on an incretin drug, about seventy-five million people. The price went down, but the drug did not become free. In March 2031 the Commerce Department extended its pharmaceutical tariffs to the raw peptide and made Eli Lilly the national champion: no duty and federal loans for its new Virginia and Texas plants, in exchange for ceiling prices. The cash portal now sells semaglutide at $249 a month, tirzepatide at $299 and the starter pill at $149. Novo matched those prices and pays the duty on its Danish ingredients. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349, a number nobody pays.

That June retatrutide got a higher dose, came off allocation and went on sale at $399. The two-year trial figure was thirty percent of body weight, which is the result of surgery delivered by pen. The muscled 'Charlotte build' spread down-market, but without coaching the result looks different. Trainers call it pen-thin.

Cheaper drugs did not mean freer access. Payers learned to ration through conditions instead of exclusions. The Medicare Bridge was renewed in December 2031 at $225 a month with a $50 copay, but it now drops anyone who has not lost five percent by month six, falls below eighty percent adherence or skips the annual bone scan. Seven states run Indiana-style Medicaid waivers. New federal guidance lets employers set premiums using pharmacy adherence data, and more than half of the employers that cover the drug attach conditions. The free liraglutide at community health centres is the one programme that still asks only that patients collect their refills. Critics on both sides cite it.

The bone wave arrived as numbers, not as a scandal. In September 2031 Medicare data showed hip-fracture admissions rising for the first time in twenty years. The modelled excess is about eighteen thousand a year, mostly women and mostly people who cycle on and off. The FDA moved bone-density scanning into the warnings section, and endocrinologists began prescribing bone drugs alongside the incretin as routine. In Sun City, Arizona, retirement-community gyms run waiting lists. Then in June 2032 the FDA approved semaglutide to reduce dementia risk in older adults with diabetes or heart disease. The group most frightened of losing their memory is now also the group most likely to break a hip.

The flatness people call 'the grey' stopped being a selling point and became a complaint. A retatrutide study confirmed it in 2031 and the label now says so. Nearly half of long-term users take deliberate breaks from their dose, and because coverage depends on adherence, many keep collecting refills they do not inject. That same month the FDA approved a low-dose pill for binge eating, and the ads promise to 'quiet the noise around food.'

The state now treats the drug as readiness infrastructure. The Pentagon offers tirzepatide to soldiers who fail the tape test, and about 140,000 are on it. Separations for body composition have fallen by nearly a third. Big-city police contracts cover it as well. Chaplains have forwarded about nineteen hundred religious objections.

Those objections belong to a wider counter-movement. In Grand Rapids church networks, and then in Nashville and Tulsa, 'Open Table' suppers serve full plates as fellowship. Fat-liberation supper clubs in Oakland advertise themselves as unmedicated. Tennessee and Idaho now bar employers from tying premiums to the drug. Meanwhile spirits volumes have fallen for a fourth year, snack makers keep selling brands, and gyms fill with people sent by a referral slip. From the outside the country looks leaner, calmer and more compliant.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Staff Sergeant Ramon Pruitt steps on the scale at Womack at 0630. The medic tapes his waist, reads the number aloud and taps the tablet. Green. Two more greens and he comes off the Metabolic Readiness list, though nobody comes off the pen.

He injects on Sundays: tirzepatide, issued at the pharmacy window, no copay. He skipped the last one. Kayla's sister was getting married in Raleigh, and he wanted to taste the brisket. The fill was picked up anyway. Everyone picks up.

At the motor pool Specialist Duarte is telling the bay that he filed the religious paperwork. His pastor wrote the letter. Somebody laughs, and somebody else doesn't.

At lunch Ramon eats half a burrito and wraps the rest, the way he has for a year.

His mother calls from Fayetteville at four. Her bone scan is Thursday. If she skips it, Medicare stops paying for the shot she takes for her memory. Fifty dollars a month. She broke her wrist in March getting out of the tub. 'I remember everything,' she says. 'That's the joke.'

At home Kayla has carried four casseroles in from the car for tonight's Open Table at the church. She is not on anything and hasn't been since Wren was born. She puts a full plate in front of him without a word.

Ramon eats all of it, slowly, and tastes the pepper. Then he feels the old pull for a second plate. It is loud, and he had forgotten it.

Wren, six, watches him chew.
